definition_en: the quality of always behaving or performing in a similar way; agreement between parts
example: Consistency in daily practice is essential for language learners.
collocations: consistency of/in; maintain/ensure consistency; lack of consistency

definition_en: happening or existing at the end of a process or period of time
example: The eventual outcome of the experiment surprised the researchers.
collocations: eventual outcome/success/failure; the eventual winner; an eventual collapse

definition_en: regularly or often
example: This error occurs frequently in first drafts of essays.
collocations: occur frequently; frequently asked; more/less frequently

definition_en: existing or coming before in time or order; previous
example: Applicants need prior experience in academic writing.
collocations: prior to; prior experience/knowledge; prior approval

definition_en: before the proper or expected time
example: It is unwise to conclude prematurely before all evidence is reviewed.
collocations: die prematurely; conclude prematurely; prematurely announce

definition_cn: 临近的；接近的；正在靠近
definition_en: coming nearer in time or space; present participle of approach
example: With the approaching deadline, the team worked overtime.
collocations: approaching deadline; approaching the problem; rapidly approaching

definition_en: a feeling of worry, nervousness, or unease
example: Exam anxiety can affect even well-prepared candidates.
collocations: anxiety about/over; cause/reduce anxiety; high levels of anxiety

definition_en: a heavy burden; something that makes progress difficult
example: Excess bureaucracy can become a dead weight on innovation.
collocations: a dead weight on; become a dead weight; carry a dead weight

definition_cn: 利益；方面（常用于 on behalf of）
definition_en: used in 'on behalf of' to mean as a representative of someone
example: She accepted the award on behalf of the whole research team.
collocations: on behalf of; on sb's behalf; speak/act on behalf of

definition_en: to last longer than something else
example: Well-built infrastructure can outlast short-term political cycles.
collocations: outlast competitors; outlast a crisis; outlast expectations

definition_en: to live or last longer than someone or something
example: Some technologies outlive the companies that created them.
collocations: outlive sb/sth; outlive its usefulness; outlive expectations

definition_cn: 意味着；打算（mean 的过去式/过去分词）
definition_en: past tense/past participle of mean: intended or signified
example: The policy was meant to reduce inequality, not increase it.
collocations: meant to do; meant that; was meant for

definition_en: plural of decade: periods of ten years
example: Air quality has improved over recent decades in many cities.
collocations: for decades; over/in recent decades; lasting decades

definition_en: used to single out an individual member of a group; special or specific
example: One particular factor explains most of the variation.
collocations: in particular; a particular case; of particular importance

definition_en: situated directly below; on the lower side
example: Underneath the optimistic report were several serious risks.
collocations: underneath the surface; lie underneath; from underneath

definition_en: to make someone believe that something is true
example: The data convinced policymakers that reform was necessary.
collocations: convince sb of/that; be convinced that; fail to convince

definition_en: a real or imagined line that marks the limit of something
example: There is a fine boundary between confidence and arrogance.
collocations: cross/push the boundary; national boundary; clear boundaries

definition_cn: 呈现；提出；造成（present 的第三人称单数）
definition_en: third-person singular of present: to show, offer, or cause something to appear
example: Climate change presents a major challenge to coastal cities.
collocations: presents a challenge/problem; presents evidence; presents an opportunity

definition_en: a judgement reached after considering evidence; the end of something
example: The study draws the conclusion that exercise improves concentration.
collocations: draw/reach a conclusion; come to the conclusion that; in conclusion

definition_en: a set of circumstances in which one finds oneself
example: In this situation, cooperation is more effective than competition.
collocations: in a situation; current/difficult situation; assess the situation

definition_en: clearly defined or identified; relating to a particular thing
example: Please give a specific example to support your argument.
collocations: specific to; a specific example; be more specific

definition_en: the quality of being helpful or practical
example: Researchers debated the usefulness of the new survey method.
collocations: the usefulness of; practical usefulness; question/doubt the usefulness

definition_en: to succeed in doing or reaching something by effort
example: Students must work consistently to achieve high scores.
collocations: achieve a goal/aim; achieve success; hard to achieve

definition_en: an area of a country or the world with common features
example: Unemployment remains high in the northern region.
collocations: in/across the region; coastal/remote region; regional differences

definition_en: the quality of being different or diverse; a number of different things
example: The course offers a variety of assessment methods.
collocations: a variety of; wide/great variety; variety in/of

definition_en: fitting in well with a person's needs or plans; easy to use
example: Online banking is convenient for people who travel frequently.
collocations: convenient for sb; at a convenient time; highly convenient

definition_cn: 最终一致性（各副本随时间最终达到一致）
definition_en: a data state in which updates propagate over time until all replicas agree
example: Distributed databases often trade strong consistency for eventual consistency.
collocations: achieve/guarantee eventual consistency; eventual consistency model

definition_en: a typical example or pattern of something; a model of how things are understood
example: Online learning has become a new paradigm in higher education.
collocations: a new/dominant paradigm; paradigm shift; within/outside the paradigm

definition_cn: 无处不在的；普遍存在的
definition_en: present, appearing, or found everywhere
example: Smartphones have become ubiquitous in everyday life.
collocations: become ubiquitous; ubiquitous in/across; nearly/almost ubiquitous

definition_en: a standard by which something is judged
example: One criterion is accuracy.
collocations: a/the criterion for; meet/satisfy a criterion; selection criterion

definition_en: likely to change; a factor that can change
example: Temperature is a key variable in the experiment.
collocations: key/independent variable; highly variable; control a variable

definition_en: a system of ideas intended to explain something
example: Darwin's theory of evolution.
collocations: theory of; in theory; put forward/propose a theory

definition_en: sufficiently great or important to be worthy of attention
example: There has been a significant improvement.
collocations: significant improvement/difference; statistically significant; of significant importance

definition_en: to include as a necessary part or result
example: The job involves a lot of travel.
collocations: involve doing; be involved in; involve a lot of

definition_en: to explain the meaning of something
example: How do you interpret these results?
collocations: interpret the results/data; interpret as; difficult to interpret

definition_en: to point out or show
example: Recent studies indicate a rise in temperatures.
collocations: indicate that; recent studies indicate; clear signs indicate

definition_en: to recognize or establish as being a particular person or thing
example: Can you identify the author of this text?
collocations: identify the cause/problem; identify as; clearly identify

definition_en: an activity or purpose natural to something
example: The function of the heart is to pump blood.
collocations: the function of; perform a function; primary/main function

definition_en: a circumstance that contributes to a result
example: Cost was a major factor in their decision.
collocations: a major/key factor; factor in/into; risk/contributing factor

definition_en: facts or information indicating whether a belief is true
example: There is clear evidence of climate change.
collocations: evidence of/for; clear/strong evidence; provide/gather evidence

definition_en: to roughly calculate or judge the value
example: Experts estimate the cost at £2 million.
collocations: estimate the cost/number; rough/conservative estimate; estimate that

definition_en: to set up on a firm or permanent basis
example: They established a new research centre.
collocations: establish a link/relationship; establish a centre/company; firmly establish

definition_en: the natural world or surrounding conditions
example: Protecting the environment is crucial.
collocations: protect the environment; working/learning environment; natural environment

definition_en: the system of trade and industry of a country
example: The global economy is recovering slowly.
collocations: the global/local economy; grow/boost the economy; economy of scale

definition_en: to give out or spread over an area
example: The charity distributed food to the poor.
collocations: distribute food/resources; widely distributed; distribute evenly

definition_en: the circumstances that form the setting for an event
example: You must consider the historical context.
collocations: in/within the context of; historical/social context; put sth in context

definition_en: to be a part of a whole; to form
example: Women constitute about half of the workforce.
collocations: constitute a threat/risk; constitute about/half; constitute evidence

definition_en: to be composed or made up of
example: The committee consists of ten members.
collocations: consist of; consist mainly/largely of; consist in

definition_en: an abstract idea or general notion
example: The concept of democracy is complex.
collocations: the concept of; key/basic concept; grasp/understand a concept

definition_en: to evaluate or estimate the nature or quality of
example: Teachers assess students' progress regularly.
collocations: assess the impact/risk; assess progress; carefully assess

definition_en: a way of dealing with something; to come near
example: A new approach to teaching languages.
collocations: an approach to; take/adopt an approach; a new/innovative approach

definition_en: to examine something in detail
example: Researchers analyse the data carefully.
collocations: analyse data/results; analyse the impact; carefully/critically analyse
